planEntityVersion.name: 10.3. Instituciones públicas, gobiernos subnacionales, actores productivos y comunidades locales han fortalecido sus modelos, capacidades y mecanismos de gobernanza territorial para la gestión sostenible de ecosistemas y la transición hacia esquemas resilientes, bajos en carbono y circulares.
planEntityVersion.description: El Sistema de las Naciones Unidas brindará asistencia técnica para fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones públicas, los gobiernos subnacionales, los actores productivos y las comunidades locales en el diseño, implementación y monitoreo de modelos de gobernanza territorial que promuevan la gestión sostenible de los ecosistemas y la transición hacia sistemas productivos resilientes, bajos en carbono y circulares. La cooperación impulsará el fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de gobernanza, la planificación territorial, la gestión integrada de los recursos naturales y las capacidades técnicas para la conservación, restauración y uso sostenible de la biodiversidad y los ecosistemas, incorporando enfoques de derechos humanos, igualdad de género, participación comunitaria e interculturalidad. Asimismo, promoverá la adopción de soluciones basadas en la naturaleza, prácticas de economía circular, modelos de producción y consumo sostenibles y mecanismos de financiamiento e incentivos para fortalecer la resiliencia de los territorios y los medios de vida, contribuyendo a un desarrollo territorial más inclusivo, sostenible y resiliente, en alineación con las prioridades nacionales y la Agenda 2030.

Al 2031, el Estado mexicano, en los tres órdenes de gobierno, aborda de manera integral el vínculo entre seguridad y desarrollo, con énfasis en la construcción de paz y la prevención del delito, incluyendo el crimen organizado, de forma coordinada, eficaz, transparente, cercana a la gente y desde un enfoque de derechos humanos y seguridad humana.
planEntityVersion.description: El Sistema de las Naciones Unidas apoyará al Estado mexicano para fortalecer las políticas públicas, los marcos institucionales y las capacidades nacionales y locales que promuevan un enfoque integral de seguridad y desarrollo, basado en los derechos humanos, la seguridad humana y la construcción de paz. La cooperación impulsará estrategias de prevención de las violencias y el delito, incluido el crimen organizado, mediante el fortalecimiento de las instituciones de seguridad y justicia, la gobernanza local, la cohesión social y la resiliencia comunitaria. Asimismo, promoverá respuestas coordinadas, transparentes, inclusivas y centradas en las personas que contribuyan a reducir los factores de riesgo y las causas estructurales de la violencia, fortalecer la confianza ciudadana en las instituciones y consolidar entornos más seguros, pacíficos y sostenibles para todas las personas.

planEntityVersion.name: Efecto 1. Al 2031, todas las personas, especialmente las que enfrentan condiciones de vulnerabilidad, tendrán mayor acceso a los derechos humanos, la justicia, la verdad, la reparación, la no repetición y a un sistema integral de protección a víctimas, independientemente de su condición migratoria, con perspectiva de género, interseccionalidad e interculturalidad.
planEntityVersion.description: El Sistema de las Naciones Unidas apoyará al Estado mexicano para fortalecer los marcos normativos, las políticas públicas, las capacidades institucionales y los mecanismos de coordinación que garanticen el acceso efectivo de todas las personas, especialmente aquellas en situación de vulnerabilidad, a los derechos humanos, la justicia, la verdad, la reparación integral, las garantías de no repetición y los servicios de protección a víctimas. La cooperación promoverá sistemas de justicia más accesibles, eficaces, inclusivos y con perspectiva de género, interseccional e intercultural; fortalecerá la prevención y atención de las violaciones a los derechos humanos y de las violencias; y contribuirá a mejorar la respuesta institucional para la protección de las víctimas, independientemente de su condición migratoria, en consonancia con los estándares internacionales de derechos humanos y las prioridades nacionales de desarrollo.

planEntityVersion.name: MEDIO AMBIENTE Y CAMBIO CLIMÁTICO
planEntityVersion.description: El Área Estratégica 4: Medio Ambiente y Cambio Climático orienta la cooperación del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para apoyar la transición hacia un modelo de desarrollo ambientalmente sostenible, resiliente e inclusivo que fortalezca la acción climática, la conservación de la biodiversidad, la gestión sostenible de los recursos naturales y la reducción del riesgo de desastres. La cooperación se enfoca en fortalecer la gobernanza ambiental y climática; impulsar una transición energética justa y sistemas de producción y consumo sostenibles; promover la adaptación y mitigación frente al cambio climático; conservar y restaurar los ecosistemas y la biodiversidad; y fortalecer la resiliencia de las personas, las comunidades y las instituciones ante los impactos del cambio climático y las crisis ambientales. Mediante el fortalecimiento de capacidades, el apoyo a políticas públicas, la innovación y las alianzas estratégicas, el Área contribuye al ejercicio del derecho a un medio ambiente sano, la sostenibilidad intergeneracional y el cumplimiento de las prioridades nacionales y la Agenda 2030.

planEntityVersion.name: ECONOMÍA INCLUYENTE Y RESILIENTE
planEntityVersion.description: El Área Estratégica 3: Economía Incluyente y Resiliente orienta la cooperación del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para promover un desarrollo económico sostenible, inclusivo, resiliente e innovador que genere trabajo decente, incremente la productividad y reduzca la pobreza y las desigualdades, sin dejar a nadie atrás. La cooperación se enfoca en fortalecer mercados laborales inclusivos, con énfasis en la generación de empleo digno y la formalización; impulsar sistemas de producción agroalimentarios e industriales sostenibles y resilientes; fomentar la innovación, la transformación productiva y el desarrollo territorial; y fortalecer capacidades institucionales para una transición económica justa frente a los desafíos demográficos, tecnológicos, ambientales y climáticos. Mediante alianzas estratégicas, el fortalecimiento de capacidades y el apoyo a políticas públicas, el Área contribuye a construir una economía más competitiva, equitativa y resiliente, alineada con las prioridades nacionales y la Agenda 2030.

planEntityVersion.name: INCLUSIÓN SOCIAL E IGUALDAD SUSTANTIVA
planEntityVersion.description: El Área Estratégica 2: Inclusión Social e Igualdad Sustantiva orienta la cooperación del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para fortalecer políticas, instituciones y sistemas que garanticen el ejercicio pleno de los derechos de todas las personas en condiciones de igualdad sustantiva, sin dejar a nadie atrás. La cooperación se centra en ampliar la protección social y los sistemas de cuidados; fortalecer el acceso universal a servicios de salud, educación, alimentación, vivienda y protección social de calidad; promover la autonomía económica de las mujeres y la igualdad sustantiva; prevenir y erradicar todas las formas de violencia y discriminación; y reducir las desigualdades que afectan de manera desproporcionada a las personas en situación de pobreza, movilidad humana, discapacidad, pueblos indígenas y afromexicanos, niñas, niños, adolescentes, juventudes y otros grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad. Mediante un enfoque basado en los derechos humanos, la igualdad de género, la interculturalidad y el curso de vida, el Área contribuye al fortalecimiento del bienestar, la cohesión social y el desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible, en alineación con las prioridades nacionales y la Agenda 2030.

planEntityVersion.name: GOBERNANZA Y ESTADO DE DERECHO
planEntityVersion.description: El Área Estratégica 1: Gobernanza y Estado de Derecho orienta la cooperación del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para fortalecer un Estado democrático, inclusivo y transparente que garantice el ejercicio de los derechos humanos, el acceso a la justicia, la seguridad, la paz y la participación de todas las personas, sin discriminación. La cooperación se enfoca en fortalecer las instituciones, ampliar el espacio cívico, promover la rendición de cuentas y la participación ciudadana, consolidar sistemas de justicia y protección de víctimas más accesibles y eficaces, impulsar la prevención de la violencia y el delito desde un enfoque de desarrollo y construcción de paz, y promover una gobernanza de la movilidad humana basada en los derechos humanos y la cooperación internacional, contribuyendo al cumplimiento de la Agenda 2030 y las prioridades nacionales de México.

planEntityVersion.name: Producto Conjunto 4.1.2. Prevención de conflictos, reducción de la discriminación y cohesión social
planEntityVersion.description: Instituciones nacionales y actores comunitarios implementan mecanismos participativos de prevención de conflictos, sensibilización y educación intercultural para reducir la discriminación, xenofobia y violencias, para la convivencia pacífica y la cohesión social.

planEntityVersion.name: Producto Conjunto 3.2.2. Mecanismos financieros e incentivos verdes que promueven inversiones sostenibles y medios de vida resilientes  e inclusivos
planEntityVersion.description: Las instituciones nacionales, las instituciones financieras, y el sector privado diseñan, amplían y fortalecen mecanismos financieros e incentivos verdes que promueven inversiones sostenibles y medios de vida resilientes  e inclusivos.

Institutions are more accountable, transparent and gender-responsive, implement innovative evidence-based policies and laws at national and subnational levels, and prevent and combat corruption and transnational crime.
planEntityVersion.description:
The UN will support efforts to enhance institutional accountability, transparency, and responsiveness at all levels of government. This will include promoting international benchmarking, peer learning, and the adaptation of innovative governance approaches. The UN will advocate for strengthening of state and local government capacities to enhance service delivery and local development. This will be complemented by in-situ programming, particularly in urban areas, and SDG-based local planning, budgeting, and implementation monitoring. This will be enhanced by UN support to national authorities, including the Department of Statistics of Malaysia (DOSM), in generating, accessing, and utilizing SDG-related and other data, disaggregated by group characteristics (specifically including gender) and locality, to strengthen evidenced-based policymaking. National evaluation capacities will also be strengthened.
Support to anti-corruption efforts will include both prevention and effective enforcement of laws. The UN will promote innovative approaches harnessing digitalization and new technologies, open budgeting initiatives, while also advancing traditional accountability mechanisms such as the right to information, public reporting of corruption, and whistle-blower protections.
The UN system will also contribute to efficient, resilient, and inclusive delivery of public services by enabling digital governance through capacity building, and the transfer of technology and know- how. UN agencies will support law enforcement, including enhancing cross-border cooperation on cybercrime investigation and intelligence sharing among law enforcement agencies, as well as provide recommendations for policy development, to prevent, and counter organized and transnational crime, including trafficking in persons, smuggling of drugs, cybercrime, scamming operations and illicit financial flows.

planEntityVersion.name: Institutions and participatory mechanisms are strengthened to effectively promote inclusion and social cohesion and respond to all forms of violence (including gender-based violence), crime, exploitation, stigmatization, discrimination, and harmful practices.
planEntityVersion.description:
Recognizing the Government’s strong commitment to social harmony and national unity, the UN will contribute to the implementation of the National Unity Policy and Blueprint 2021-2030 to strengthen inter-ethnic relations, social cohesion, and trust by engaging with diverse communities and promoting interactions and exchange. Programming will support dialogue and promote innovative channels for direct engagement, with particular emphasis on women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation at all levels of decision-making and governance. 
The UN will also partner with media and civil society stakeholders to promote digital citizenship and media literacy, to counter divisive narratives, xenophobia, hate speech and misogyny and to combat discrimination and stigma.  Interventions will also seek to strengthen multisectoral responses to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, children, and persons with disabilities.
UN agencies will continue to advocate for the rights and protection of refugees, stateless people, and undocumented populations, including tailored support to mitigate stigma and exclusion. Specific attention will be given to migrant workers, including advocacy on rights, welfare, and access to services and remedies. Given the scale of the challenge, particular focus will be placed on Sabah, where a significant share of the stateless and undocumented population resides, to support durable policy responses.

planEntityVersion.name: People, especially women and children, benefit from justice and human rights protections as institutions and legal frameworks are aligned with international normative standards and function effectively.
planEntityVersion.description:
The UN will leverage its normative mandate to advocate for the realization of human rights for all, with a focus on vulnerable groups . Efforts will include advocacy for Malaysia’s accession to the six-core international human rights treaties not yet ratified, and for the reduction of reservations on the three ratified treaties (CEDAW, CRC and CRPD). UNCT will promote women’s participation in social, economic, and political life, advocate against practices that harm women and girls, and support mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment in development plans and M&E frameworks. The UN will also support the implementation of existing international commitments and obligations on women, peace and security.
Through partnerships with the private sector, the UN will promote human rights in the workplace and in the provision of goods and services, building on the work already underway during the previous CF cycle.  Complementary efforts will support the endorsement and implementation of ILO labour conventions, ensuring alignment with international labour standards.

planEntityVersion.name: Resilience of communities, women and children, and other groups most vulnerable to environmental hazards, shocks, and disasters, is strengthened by enhancing adaptive capacities and meaningful participation in decision-making and solutions.
planEntityVersion.description:
At both the strategic and operational levels, the UN will support policy and programming measures that promote greater resilience to environmental and climate-related shocks to all communities. This will include enabling policy development at the federal and state levels to advance climate-adaptive investments, strengthened climate-resilient social services and to facilitate and incentivize the building of resilience within society more broadly. UN interventions will include assisting with the adoption of new techniques within government (risk-assessment/risk proofing) and applying fiscal and regulatory instruments to manage and mitigate environmental risks. The UN will seek to enable effective coordination across levels of government and across localities, recognizing the variability of threats and vulnerabilities. 
Through partnerships with civil society, the UN will reach out to local communities to engage them in greening workplace and household practices and promoting locally tailored measures to mitigate shocks and enhance self-adaptation. Special attention will be given to the differentiated vulnerabilities of the groups most at risk, especially women, low-income households, and those facing multiple forms of exclusion. Targeted support will also focus on communities in vulnerable and geographically remote areas, including indigenous peoples and those which are resource-dependent (e.g., fishing communities).

planEntityVersion.name: Institutions are strengthened and local communities, particularly indigenous peoples, are empowered to drive sustainable, gender-responsive and inclusive natural resource and biodiversity management, and nature-based solutions.
planEntityVersion.description:
This output focuses on enhancing institutional capacity and community empowerment to support effective and equitable environmental stewardship. At the federal level, the UN will provide technical assistance to strengthen leadership, coordination, and policy implementation on urban environmental management. At the subnational level, support will be tailored to specific needs of local governments, including improving spatial planning and delivering tailored local solutions related to waste management, air quality and urban living conditions, including the preservation and provision of green spaces.
UN programming will contribute to systems strengthening and building the capacities of institutions to decarbonize, restore and protect eco-systems, and promote disaster resilience through risk-assessment and risk-proofing of infrastructure and investments. This will include strengthening of climate data for evidence-informed decision-making and environmental governance. Special emphasis will be on building the capacity of local governments to manage municipal, chemical and biomedical waste, improve the urban environment and living conditions, and integrate pollution-related risks into local public health frameworks. 
The UN will also work with the Government to leverage global and regional climate and biodiversity knowledge through inter-governmental exchange and South-South cooperation. Cross-border environmental challenges such as haze pollution, waste trafficking, and marine pollution caused by disposal of plastic debris in the ocean will be also addressed in partnerships with national and regional stakeholders.
Finally, UN agencies will seek to protect the rights of the resource-dependent communities, including indigenous peoples and local communities, promoting equitable and sustainable access to natural resources, ensuring adherence to Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. The UN will also explore and leverage the potential of traditional knowledge systems to deliver better environmental and resource management at the local level.

planEntityVersion.name: Malaysia adopts just, clean energy, low-carbon, gender-responsive and circular economy solutions, including more effectively managed waste and improved regulation of pollution.
planEntityVersion.description:
This collaborative output addresses both policy formulation and implementation of Malaysia’s green transition. At the policy level, UN support will focus on enhancing climate mitigation and adaptation strategies through the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) framework and national adaptation planning. Particular attention will be given to addressing plastic pollution, particularly within marine areas, and reversing biodiversity loss in vulnerable localities.  
At the operational level, the UN will provide technical assistance on the roll-out of clean energy, low-carbon and just transition policies, as well as policies related to waste management and pollution control. These will include the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies, application of circular economy models, and improved environmental planning and regulation at subnational levels across all sectors. 
Additionally, industry-level efforts will focus on high-impact sectors, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, and electric mobility, while embedding just transition principles to protect workers and communities affected by the ongoing shifts in energy production and consumption.  The UN will advocate for improved environmental stewardship across enterprises, including MSMEs, by promoting low-carbon practices, ESG-aligned investments, and circular economy solutions.

planEntityVersion.name: Infrastructures and investments are more equitable, recognizing the needs of urban and rural areas, and communities at risk of being left behind.
planEntityVersion.description:
Spatial and group-based inequalities, such as between urban and rural areas, core, and peripheral regions and vis a vis groups at risk of being left behind, remain among Malaysia’s most pressing development challenges. Some 75 per cent of the population live in cities, and there is growing urban sprawl and urban-rural gaps.  These disparities undermine inclusive growth and risk constraining the country’s HIC transition. While Government’s efforts are underway to address these imbalances, a more data-driven, inclusive, and spatially sensitive approach is required to ensure more equitable development outcomes. 
In response, the UN will support efforts to strengthen national and subnational data systems and analytical capacities to better identify and track geographic and demographic disparities.  This evidence base will inform more responsive and inclusive policymaking, particularly in relation to infrastructure development, service provision, and public investment. These efforts are especially pertinent to regional and local planning initiatives, addressing spatial disparities.
Indeed, complementing this, the UN programming will promote and enable greater investments in underserved regions and for vulnerable populations. This includes supporting initiatives to reduce rural-urban divides, address disparities between Malaysia’s core and lagging states, and help enhance infrastructure provision and services to groups at risk of being left behind.

planEntityVersion.name: Productivity and competitiveness, particularly of MSMEs, are enhanced as Malaysia transitions to a digital and green high-income economy with a fair and transparent business environment which promotes SDG-aligned investments
planEntityVersion.description:
Malaysia’s productivity growth and competitiveness, especially among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) remain constrained by structural and capacity-related challenges. This output focuses on addressing these constraints through targeted support to enhance enterprise performance, enabling broader economic transformation. Interventions will include improved technology transfer, labour reskilling, and better access to finance and trade opportunities. The explicit linking of productivity and competitiveness gains with greener and more inclusive business models will be a dimension of the UN’s approach. 
The UN will seek to deliver this, by supporting the take-up of ESG practices and investments particularly by MSMEs and securing wider SDG compliance via the realignment of business incentives, in particular in the context of the forthcoming National ESG Strategic Plan, a ten-year plan envisioned to take Malaysian business entities beyond ESG compliance, and drive competitive advantage. In the social and governance spheres, this includes the business and human rights agenda, and in the environmental sphere, improving resource and energy efficiency, and facilitating access to new technologies and markets, such as those related to electric vehicles, renewable energy, and artificial intelligence. 

To enable these shifts, the UN will provide technical support for policy reforms aimed at creating a more supportive operating environment, including appropriate incentive structures to encourage improvements in productivity and competitiveness alongside SDG objectives. This involves supporting and accelerating current government reforms and tackling key bottlenecks, particularly to MSME expansion, notably, access to finance and trade opportunities for all sectors, including agri-commodities. The UN’s work will also include supporting the scaling up of (this is as mentioned in RMK13) MSMEs, particularly to access green financing, foster sustainable business practices and enable their integration into global green supply chains.

planEntityVersion.name: The labour market provides demand-driven opportunities, enhances women’s economic participation, enables reskilling and upskilling, and protects rights for all with a focus on caregivers, migrant workers, persons with disabilities, youth, and women.
planEntityVersion.description:
Recognizing the central role of employment in driving inclusive growth, this output supports efforts to address persistent labour market disparities and barriers to decent work. Particular attention is given to the economic participation of women, whose labour force participation continues to lag significantly behind, as well as to groups which are disadvantaged in the labour market. 
UN programming and advocacy will promote gender-responsive labour policies and workplace rights, while supporting the development of a more inclusive and demand-driven skills economy.  This includes strengthening the TVET architecture, ensuing that it is better aligned with the evolving needs of industry, and closing skills gaps, particularly in digital, green, and new technologies. A core focus will be on enhancing productivity and enabling access to higher-value employment for women and youth. 
To advance broader inclusion and equity, UN interventions will support the creation of enabling work environments for persons with disabilities, as well as address the employment challenges faced by informal sector workers and migrants. In addition, the UN will also address systemic drivers of child labour in specific sectors. Environmental sustainability will be promoted as an integral part of this transition, including efforts to green the workplace and mainstream just transition principles across labour market reforms.

planEntityVersion.name: Food and nutrition systems meet the needs of all people in Malaysia, address undernutrition and obesity, specifically among women, children, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntityVersion.description:
Malaysia faces a triple burden of malnutrition challenge with the coexistence of undernutrition and stunting, especially among children, alongside rising rates of obesity and micronutrient deficiency. These trends reflect both structural inequities and changing consumption patterns linked to rapid economic growth and urbanization. The burden is not evenly distributed, with significant disparities across geographic regions and population groups, requiring disaggregated, equity-sensitive approaches. 
In response, the UN will support the development of integrated, sustainable, and locally adapted food and nutrition systems and policies. Interventions will promote access to sufficient, affordable, and nutritious food while addressing behavioural, cultural and socioeconomic determinants of poor diets. The UN will also contribute to strengthening national capacities in food systems governance, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and multi-sector coordination.

planEntityVersion.name: The social protection system is strengthened to provide universal coverage throughout the lifecycle, especially for people in vulnerable situations.
planEntityVersion.description: Malaysia’s social protection system faces two primary challenges: incomplete lifecycle coverage for the general population and inadequate provision for individuals with heightened or overlapping vulnerabilities, such as men and women with disabilities, children, older persons, and people living in poverty. These gaps reduce the system’s capacity to mitigate risks and shocks, enable equitable access and effectively address fragmentation, thereby weakening human capital, limiting inclusive economic growth, and contributing to intergenerational cycles of disadvantage, with adverse impacts on nutrition, health, and well-being.  Malaysia is well-positioned to embrace a progressive universality model in strengthening its Social Protection Floor (SPF), to ensure that all citizens, particularly the most vulnerable populations, have access to essential benefits that secure their fundamental rights to health, income, and well-being.

planEntityVersion.name: The healthcare system is more resilient and better capacitated to deliver universal access to care, promote well-being and healthy ageing, and address population-specific risk factors.
planEntityVersion.description: This collaborative output supports both the strengthening of national health systems and their ability to deliver equitable, quality care across the life cycle for all communities. UN agencies will align their work with Malaysia’s Health White Paper (2023), focusing on the development of a health system that is adequately financed, equitable and affordable. The UN will contribute to system resilience by supporting infrastructure, service continuity and fiscal strategies that balance public health financing with reduced out of pocket costs. Informed by the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, the UN will also assist in building preparedness capacities for future public health emergencies.

planEntityVersion.name: Access to inclusive quality and values-based education is improved for all children and young people.
planEntityVersion.description: This collaborative output addresses two interrelated challenges: gaps in mainstream education, including concerns about quality of attainment and increasing social polarization, and the difficulties faced by some non-citizen children in accessing schooling. This latter group includes undocumented and stateless children (particularly in Sabah) as well as refugees, where civil society and the UN often play a critical role in service provision. These educational disparities have far-reaching implications, given the central role of human capital development in national economic transformation and the importance of education in the socialization of values and promotion of social cohesion.

planEntityVersion.name: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
planEntityVersion.description: This outcome focuses on strengthening governance systems and institutional capacities in line with the international human rights standards and normative frameworks. It reflects the Government’s overarching emphasis, as articulated in the Thirteenth Plan, on institutional reform as a core pillar of Malaysia’s development pathway and its forthcoming HIC transition. In this context, UN support aims to help Malaysia embed and uphold global standards of peace and security, the rule of law, human rights, transparency and accountability across all levels of governance, including as part of the efforts to ensure the achievement of the SDG targets by 2030.

planEntityVersion.name: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
planEntityVersion.description: This outcome addresses the in-country impacts of the triple planetary crisis (climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution). It reflects growing vulnerabilities of Malaysia’s natural environment to extreme weather events, and rising temperatures and sea levels. These risks are driven by global environmental dynamics and intensified by Malaysia’s rapid economic trajectory, increasing energy needs, growing consumption, and continued fossil fuel dependence.

planEntityVersion.name: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
planEntityVersion.description: The outcome statement for SPA 2 focuses on inclusive and sustainable economic transformation. It envisions a high-income economy that is future-ready, resilient and environmentally sustainable, driving broad-based growth and enabling opportunities for all, particularly, women, youth and populations in lagging regions. Economic transformation is approached not only in terms of growth maximization, but of structural change that enhances equity, sustainability and productivity in high value-added sectors focused on technology but also including high-value service industries (notably tourism). This includes diversifying the economy through innovation and digitalization by leveraging the Malaysia Digital initiatives to promote the growth of these digital industries, facilitating a green transition, helping to create decent jobs and more functional labour market and expanding economic participation and opportunity via targeted investments.

planEntityVersion.name: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
planEntityVersion.description: The outcome statement for SPA 1 centres on inclusive social development and well-being. This is defined by equitable access to quality social services and the realization of basic human capabilities, as outlined in the relevant SDGs and international human rights instruments. Key dimensions include education, health, social protection, and food and nutrition, with the aim of enabling all people living in Malaysia to realise their full human potentials.

planEntityVersion.name: Governance, Participation, Rights and Social Cohesion
Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
Economic Transformation for Inclusive and Sustainable Prosperity
Inclusive Social Development & Well-Being
Las instituciones a nivel central y local fortalecen los mecanismos de coordinación para prevenir la violencia, promover la cohesión social y fortalecer la resiliencia.
Actores clave implementan sistemas de gobernanza innovadora, interoperabilidad institucional y uso estratégico de datos para la toma de decisiones inclusivas y basadas en evidencia.

Las instituciones públicas fortalecen sus capacidades para ofrecer bienes y servicios accesibles, eficientes y con enfoque de derechos, incluyendo justicia y seguridad, promoviendo el acceso a información pública.

Personas en situación de vulnerabilidad, especialmente mujeres, niños, niñas y jóvenes, están empoderadas para ejercer sus derechos y participar activamente en los procesos de gobernanza y monitoreo de políticas públicas.

Instituciones y socios clave diseñan, implementan y evalúan políticas sociales, planes y programas intersectoriales que promuevan el piso de protección social con enfoque territorial, de derechos humanos, de género y ciclo de vida.

Instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales están fortalecidas y cuentan con las capacidades humanas, financieras, y los sistemas para ofrecer bienes y servicios de calidad, basados en derechos, con enfoque de género, con sensibilidad y pertinencia cultural.

Personas en situación de vulnerabilidad —especialmente mujeres, niños, niñas y jóvenes— reciben información culturalmente pertinente sobre sus derechos y los bienes y servicios sociales disponibles, participan activamente en espacios de consulta para el desarrollo de políticas públicas, y acceden de manera efectiva a dichos servicios.

Instituciones y socios claves promueven inversiones alineadas a los acuerdos ambientales multilaterales y marcos normativos que fomentan la economía circular y creativa, infraestructura resiliente, sistemas alimentarios sostenibles y gestión sostenible de recursos naturales.

Comunidades y gobiernos locales adoptan prácticas sostenibles que fortalecen los medios de vida, la resiliencia frente al cambio climático, preservación de la biodiversidad, gestión de los desechos y reducción de riesgos de desastres.

Instituciones y socios claves formulan e implementan políticas que impulsan la productividad, el acceso a mercados, economía sostenible y creativa, así como la innovación en sectores estratégico para facilitar la transición digital y ambiental de manera inclusiva.
Socios claves implementan mecanismos para la gestión integral equitativa, transparente y sostenible de los recursos naturales, biodiversidad y los ecosistemas estratégicos.

Personas en situación de vulnerabilidad, especialmente mujeres y jóvenes, acceden a formación técnica, programas de voluntariado y capacitación laboral orientados a sectores sostenibles, incluyendo agricultura familiar y economía circular.

Para 2030, Panamá contará con una gobernanza fortalecida, descentralizada, con instituciones más eficaces, accesibles a la población, interconectadas y con sistemas de información robustos, que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios públicos, incluyendo la justicia, y que contribuyan a la cohesión social y prevengan y reduzcan la violencia y la conflictividad, logrando sociedades y territorios seguros, pacíficos y resilientes a nivel nacional y local, donde todas las personas, especialmente mujeres y grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, gozan plenamente de sus derechos.
planEntityVersion.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para lograr este resultado, tres condiciones fundamentales deben estar presentes:
Primero, más personas, especialmente mujeres y grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, deben conocer y ejercer plenamente sus derechos; participar activamente y de forma informada en los procesos de gobernanza, planificación y monitoreo de políticas públicas; acceder a servicios de calidad, incluyendo justicia, con enfoque de derechos; y contribuir al fortalecimiento institucional y la cohesión social.
Segundo, las instituciones deben ser fuertes, modernas, inclusivas y centradas en las personas, operando con eficiencia, transparencia y participación, garantizando el acceso a servicios, justicia y seguridad, y asignando recursos públicos de forma eficiente y equitativa, basándose en evidencia y en resultados.
Y tercero, debe consolidarse una gobernanza moderna mediante la actualización normativa, la digitalización e innovación, mejora de la infraestructura pública, fortalecimiento de capacidades, uso estratégico de datos, coordinación institucional efectiva y diseño de políticas públicas inclusivas y basadas en evidencia para construir territorios seguros, resilientes y cohesionados.

planEntityVersion.name: Para 2030, más personas, especialmente las que están en situación de vulnerabilidad, acceden a servicios sociales básicos de calidad, sostenibles, con pertinencia cultural y territorial, y con enfoque de género, que contribuyen a cerrar brechas estructurales y a garantizar el ejercicio pleno de sus derechos.
planEntityVersion.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para alcanzar este resultado, deben cumplirse tres condiciones clave:
Primero, más personas en situación de vulnerabilidad, incluyendo niñas, niños, adolescentes, mujeres, pueblos indígenas, afrodescendientes, personas con discapacidad, migrantes, refugiadas, solicitantes de la condición de refugiado, apátridas, personas mayores y LGBTIQ+, deben tener acceso a información sobre sus derechos, conocer los servicios disponibles y transformarse las normas sociales discriminatorias que dificultan ese acceso.

Segundo, las instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales (salud, educación, protección, agua, cuidados, etc.) deben ser resilientes y fortalecidas, contar con personal capacitado y presupuesto suficiente, e implementar sistemas como registros únicos sensibles a poblaciones clave y nuevos instrumentos de medición que garanticen cobertura en zonas rurales, comarcas y albergues.

Tercero, se deben diseñar e implementar políticas públicas intersectoriales inclusivas acompañadas de mecanismos de coordinación, articulación institucional y planificación e inversión pública con enfoque territorial y de inclusión social.

planEntityVersion.name: Más personas, especialmente poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, mujeres y jóvenes, participan activamente y se benefician de una transformación económica y transición justa, inclusiva y sostenible, que prioriza la resiliencia climática, las soluciones basadas en la naturaleza y la protección de la diversidad natural y cultural de Panamá, al tiempo que promueve la diversificación económica, con enfoque de circularidad, que cree empleos y trabajo decente y reduce la contaminación y generación de desechos.
planEntityVersion.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para lograr este resultado, deben cumplirse al menos cinco condiciones clave:
Primero, se requiere invertir en capital humano mediante formación técnica, voluntariado y capacitación laboral, garantizando oportunidades para mujeres, jóvenes y otras poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, fortaleciendo la agricultura familiar y estimulando la transición de la economía informal al trabajo decente.
Segundo, todos los actores relevantes deben invertir en la gestión integral, equitativa, transparente y sostenible del capital natural, colocando el agua y la biodiversidad como bienes públicos estratégicos y promoviendo la conservación y restauración de ecosistemas.
Tercero, las instituciones deben formular e implementar políticas de desarrollo humano participativas e inclusivas que fortalezcan la productividad, el acceso a mercados y la innovación en sectores clave como la economía digital, las energías limpias, el turismo sostenible y la bioeconomía
Cuarto, es necesario adoptar prácticas sostenibles que generen capacidad adaptativa frente al cambio climático, la pérdida de biodiversidad, los desastres y la contaminación, promoviendo un crecimiento resiliente y regenerativo.
Y quinto, se deben promover inversiones alineadas con los Acuerdos Multilaterales Ambientales y marcos normativos que integren economía circular, infraestructura resiliente y gestión sostenible de recursos naturales, contemplando las necesidades de los más vulnerables con enfoque territorial.

planEntityVersion.name: Buena gobernanza, participativa y eficiente, seguridad y fortalecimiento institucional, con enfoque de derechos
planEntityVersion.description:
La visión nacional, expresada en el PEG 2025–2029, es: "Volver a convertir a Panamá en un país más próspero y seguro, con más dinero en el bolsillo de la gente, más crecimiento y pleno empleo. Y sentir el orgullo de que Panamá sea la economía de mayor crecimiento de toda América Latina". La visión del Marco de Cooperación se enmarca en esta aspiración nacional: "Entonces todas las personas en Panamá, especialmente las que están más afectadas por la desigualdad, disfrutan de una prosperidad equitativa, resiliente y sostenible, facilitada por una buena gobernanza democrática y participativa".
Para que esta visión de cambio se materialice, se debe cumplir con la siguiente condicion clave: que las instituciones están fortalecidas y son modernas, eficientes, eficaces, transparentes y participativas, desde el nivel nacional hasta el local, garantizan el acceso a la justicia, seguridad y potencian la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia y centrada en las personas y sus derechos humanos.

planEntityVersion.name: Servicios sociales básicos de calidad, equitativos, resilientes e inclusivos
planEntityVersion.description:
La visión nacional, expresada en el PEG 2025–2029, es: "Volver a convertir a Panamá en un país más próspero y seguro, con más dinero en el bolsillo de la gente, más crecimiento y pleno empleo. Y sentir el orgullo de que Panamá sea la economía de mayor crecimiento de toda América Latina". La visión del Marco de Cooperación se enmarca en esta aspiración nacional: "Entonces todas las personas en Panamá, especialmente las que están más afectadas por la desigualdad, disfrutan de una prosperidad equitativa, resiliente y sostenible, facilitada por una buena gobernanza democrática y participativa".

Para que esta visión de cambio se materialice, se debe cumplir con la siguiente condiciones clave: Que todas las personas, especialmente quienes se quedan atrás, tienen acceso a servicios básicos de calidad, sostenibles, con pertinencia cultural, enfoque territorial y de género, y las instituciones son resilientes y cuentan con personal capacitado y presupuesto suficiente, basado en resultados y evidencias.

planEntityVersion.name: Crecimiento, desarrollo sostenible y resiliente con generación de trabajo decente
planEntityVersion.description:
La visión nacional, expresada en el PEG 2025–2029, es: "Volver a convertir a Panamá en un país más próspero y seguro, con más dinero en el bolsillo de la gente, más crecimiento y pleno empleo. Y sentir el orgullo de que Panamá sea la economía de mayor crecimiento de toda América Latina". La visión del Marco de Cooperación se enmarca en esta aspiración nacional: "Entonces todas las personas en Panamá, especialmente las que están más afectadas por la desigualdad, disfrutan de una prosperidad equitativa, resiliente y sostenible, facilitada por una buena gobernanza democrática y participativa".

Para que esta visión de cambio se materialice, se debe cumplir con la siguiente situación clave: lograr un crecimiento económico y un desarrollo sostenible y resiliente con respeto al medio ambiente, que mejoren las condiciones de vida de todas las personas; a través de inversiones responsables, fortalecimiento del desarrollo humano y diseño e implementación de políticas públicas;

planEntityVersion.name: 4.2. Conflict-affected people have improved access to essential services, livelihoods and strengthened protection of human rights.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will support conflict-affected people on both sides of the dividing line by improving their access to essential services, livelihoods, and protection of human rights to support the conflict-affected populations in shaping their future in an empowered and dignified way.

planEntityVersion.name: 4.1. Space expanded for inclusive dialogue and confidence-building between divided communities, and for the inclusion of women and youth in promoting peace and security.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will work to expand space for inclusive dialogue and confidence-building between divided communities. This includes creating platforms for engagement and people-to-people contacts, supporting community-led initiatives, and ensuring that women and youth are actively involved in peace and security efforts. These interventions are designed to foster mutual understanding, reduce tensions, and build the social capital necessary for peace.

planEntityVersion.name: 3.2. Civic space, intra-societal dialogue and social cohesion are strengthened.
planEntityVersion.description:
UN will foster civic space, intra-societal dialogue, and social cohesion. This involves building the capacities of civic actors, raising public awareness, and promoting the inclusion of voices that are often marginalized. By building a culture of participation and dialogue, the UN aims to ensure that governance reflects the diversity of Georgia’s society and that all people effectively participate in decision-making processes affecting their lives. 
The rationale behind these interventions is grounded in the evidence that inclusive governance leads to more stable and peaceful societies. When people feel heard and represented, trust in institutions grows, and social cohesion is strengthened. Gender equality and human rights protections are not only moral imperatives but also essential for sustainable development. Decentralization, when effectively implemented, brings decision-making closer to communities and improves service delivery, thereby building trust between government and its citizens.

planEntityVersion.name: 3.1. National and local institutions have enhanced capacities for promoting human rights, gender equality, an inclusive and accessible justice system in line with international commitments, and for fostering inclusive governance and effective decentralization.
planEntityVersion.description:
UN will work to enhance the capacities of national and local institutions to promote human rights, gender equality, and an inclusive and accessible justice system. This includes supporting the alignment of national frameworks with the country’s international human rights commitments. 
Georgia signed and ratified most of the core UN human rights conventions. The UN system will assist the Government of Georgia in meeting its international human rights obligations and commitments, which lie at the heart of sustainable development. 
At the national level, the term ‘gender equality’ was removed from all Georgian laws and replaced by ‘equality between women and men’ in April 2025. Georgia’s international commitments on the rights of all women and girls include Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW, ratified by Georgia in 1994) and its General Recommendations, Council of Europe Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence against Women and Domestic Violence (Istanbul Convention, ratified by Georgia in 2017), Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action, outcome documents of the Commission of the Status of Women, and the SDGs, especially Goal 5, which calls for achieving gender equality and empowering all women and girls. 
The UN will work to strengthen the capacity of key institutions to uphold human rights and will facilitate multi-stakeholder dialogues and partnerships on human rights issues. To do so, the UN’s support will be framed by the recommendations of the human rights mechanisms available to Georgia, in particular as a result of the upcoming 4th cycle of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) in 2026. National priorities in the area of human rights protection were outlined in the National Strategy for the Protection of Human Rights in Georgia 2022-2030, and related action plans, which will continue to inform UN’s support to Georgia. 
Furthermore, by equipping institutions with the competencies and policy tools they need, the UN will contribute to a governance environment that is more transparent, accountable, and inclusive. Leveraging the UN’s strong programmatic experience, such efforts can contribute to strengthening inclusion and sustainability of development progress at the local level.

planEntityVersion.name: 2.3. The social protection system has improved capacities to identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks, thereby reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities for all.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will support the development of a social protection system that can identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks. This system must be capable of reaching all individuals—including asylum seekers, refugees, migrants, older persons and people with special needs— at any point throughout their lives. It must also provide protection in the workplace, support survivors of violence, and deliver services effectively at the local level. The implementation of the biopsychosocial model of disability will require additional resources and efforts, but has the potential to transform the lives of people with disabilities. These interventions are critical to reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities and ensuring that social protection is proactive, inclusive and universal.

planEntityVersion.name: 2.2. Capacities of institutions and service providers are enhanced to deliver inclusive quality health and social services, address key health risks, promote well-being, and reach the most vulnerable.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will work to enhance the capacities of institutions and service providers to deliver inclusive, quality health and social services by strengthening universal health coverage, primary health care and continue medical education systems, improving mental health support, promoting healthy lifestyles, and reaching underserved communities through innovative approaches, such as telemedicine and other digital innovative products. These efforts are based on the understanding that health outcomes are shaped by several factors, including behavioural and environmental ones. Promoting well-being requires coordinated action across sectors and sustained investment in both infrastructure and human resources.

planEntityVersion.name: 2.1. The education system has increased capacities to deliver accessible, inclusive and life-long quality education and training.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will support the education system to increase its capacity to deliver accessible, inclusive, and lifelong quality education and training. This includes expanding outreach, integrating health and personal safety education, and improving school-to-work transitions. These interventions are designed to reduce disparities, particularly in rural areas, and to align education more closely with labour market needs. A more inclusive education system that can respond to the needs of children with disabilities and other marginalized groups is foundational to breaking cycles of poverty and exclusion.

planEntityVersion.name: 1.4. National and local institutions and communities have adequate capacities and tools to advance environmental governance, protect biodiversity, manage natural resources sustainably, and reduce pollution.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will support national and local institutions in advancing environmental governance, protecting biodiversity, managing natural resources sustainably, and reducing pollution. These actions contribute to a cleaner environment and support the creation of green jobs, aligning economic growth with environmental sustainability.

planEntityVersion.name: 1.3. Capacities of institutions and communities are enhanced for inclusive climate action, disaster risk reduction, and resilient, risk-informed development.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will enhance the capacities of institutions and communities for inclusive climate action and disaster risk reduction. This involves building resilience and preparedness at multiple levels and integrating risk-informed planning into development strategies. These measures are critical for protecting economic gains from climate-related shocks and for enabling sustainable rural expansion.

planEntityVersion.name: 1.2. Relevant institutions, rural communities and businesses have enhanced capacities to promote and participate in a diversified, green, competitive, and inclusive rural economy, and in sustainable agri-food systems.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will strengthen the capacities of institutions, rural communities, and businesses to participate in a diversified, green, and inclusive rural economy. This includes support for climate-smart agriculture, expanding economic opportunities for farmers and the development of sustainable agri-food systems. By improving productivity and competitiveness in global food markets, these interventions aim to revitalize rural economies and reduce regional disparities. These should be supported by complementary actions such as land consolidation and market access.

planEntityVersion.name: 1.1: Improved enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable and digital economic development, delivering decent jobs, more competitive MSMEs, and fostering women’s economic empowerment.
planEntityVersion.description: UN will work to improve the enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable, and digital economic development. This involves strengthening national, local and social partners’ institutions to develop inclusive labour policies and better protection of workers’ rights, as well as enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs. The UN will foster innovation, digitalization, connectivity, and sustainable value chains. These efforts are expected to generate decent jobs and empower women economically, particularly by recognizing and addressing the care economy, which remains a significant barrier to women’s full participation in the labour market.

planEntityVersion.name: OUTCOME 4: AN ENABLING ENVIRONMENT FOR PEACE
planEntityVersion.description:
OUTCOME 4: BY 2030, PEOPLE AFFECTED BY CONFLICT, INCLUDING IDPS, ENJOY ENHANCED ENGAGEMENT, TRUST, AND RESILIENCE FOR AN ENABLING ENVIRONMENT FOR PEACE, ACROSS DIVIDING LINES
This outcome addresses the legacy of unresolved conflict and the resulting social fragmentation, displacement and marginalization on the ground. It highlights the importance of a concerted effort to support populations affected by conflict to ensure that no one is left behind and improve enabling environment of lasting peace. No geographic distinction is made regarding conflict-affected communities, and the term encompasses people in all of Georgia, on either side of the dividing line, including IDPs (with or without official status), and particularly communities adjacent to the dividing line.

planEntityVersion.name: OUTCOME 3: GOVERNANCE, HUMAN RIGHTS, GENDER EQUALITY AND SOCIAL COHESION
planEntityVersion.description:
OUTCOME 3: BY 2030, PEOPLE IN GEORGIA BENEFIT FROM A MORE DECENTRALIZED AND INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE SYSTEM, WITH STRONGER HUMAN RIGHTS PROTECTIONS, GENDER EQUALITY, AND ENHANCED SOCIAL COHESION.
This Outcome envisions a society where governance is not only more decentralized but also more inclusive, participatory and rights-based. Achieving this requires both stronger national and local institutions that are more capable, accountable, and responsive, as well as support to the people of Georgia in becoming more empowered, informed, and engaged.

planEntityVersion.name: OUTCOME 2: EDUCATION, HEALTH AND SOCIAL PROTECTION
planEntityVersion.description:
OUTCOME 2: BY 2030, PEOPLE IN GEORGIA ENJOY IMPROVED LEARNING OUTCOMES, HEALTHIER LIVES AND REDUCED VULNERABILITIES, SUPPORTED BY COMPREHENSIVE SOCIAL PROTECTION, THEREBY BRIDGING THE RURAL-URBAN DIVIDE
This outcome reflects the concept of human development where education, health, and social protection are interdependent pillars of well-being, inclusion and empowerment. By contributing to this outcome, the UN in Georgia aims at supporting the country in shifting towards inclusive, accessible, and resilient systems that respond to the diverse needs of the population across the life cycle. This will also foster demographic resilience as discussed under Outcome 1.

planEntityVersion.name: OUTCOME 1: INCLUSIVE GROWTH, GREEN TRANSITION AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE
planEntityVersion.description:
OUTCOME 1: BY 2030, PEOPLE IN GEORGIA, ESPECIALLY THOSE LIVING IN RURAL AREAS, BENEFIT FROM A GROWING, MORE DIVERSIFIED, GREEN AND INCLUSIVE ECONOMY, AND A HEALTHIER ENVIRONMENT MORE RESILIENT TO CLIMATE CHANGE AND NATURAL HAZARDS
This Outcome reflects a holistic development vision that integrates inclusive economic growth and environmental sustainability. It acknowledges that in Georgia people in rural areas require targeted support as they currently have fewer pathways to benefit from economic opportunities and are more immediately affected by environmental degradation and climate change. It also implies placing low-emission and climate-resilient agriculture at the centre of rural development and integrated value chain development, including in non-agricultural sectors. Other important structural challenges addressed by this Outcome include the relatively large share of workers in the informal sector, the low participation of women in the labour market, and the high proportion of youth not in employment, education or training.

planEntityVersion.name: PROMOTING GREEN AND INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT TO REDUCE RURAL-URBAN DIVIDE
planEntityVersion.description:
The overall theory of change for Georgia’s progress towards the SDGs is premised on the interconnectedness of the main components of the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development, and more specifically People, Prosperity, Planet, Partnership, and Peace. Recognizing that sustainable economic growth is inseparable from environmental protection and climate action, this Framework positions these priorities as a unified and essential pillar of its theory of change. It embraces green growth not only as a necessity but as a powerful opportunity to create decent work and sustainable livelihoods. 
Neither the economy nor the planet can truly thrive if the people who inhabit it are unable to realize their full potential throughout their lives. In the context of Georgia, this means ensuring that all people, wherever they live, can expand their learning outcomes, live healthier lives and be supported by a comprehensive social protection system. Lifelong learning opportunities will also ensure that people, especially youth and older people, have the skills required by an evolving labour market, supporting economic development and inclusion. 
To reduce the urban-rural divide and support Georgia in its efforts to maintain peace and foster social cohesion, the change pathway includes furthering decentralization to make service delivery more efficient and well-targeted at the local level and bring the decision-making closer to the people; enhancing access to effective justice and remedies to ensure that all individuals receive legal support and fair treatment; and strengthening the rule of law and reducing social tensions. Establishing strong human rights institutions that operate with transparency and accountability is also considered essential to safeguard freedoms and enforce protections, thus leading to greater social cohesion. Likewise, strengthening legal tools and promoting behavioural change for gender equality will enable greater women’s participation in public life. Expanding the civic space and fostering participatory systems would allow for more meaningful public engagement, leading to more efficient, accountable decision-making and a sense of shared responsibility that can catalyse progress, promote inclusion and reduce social divides.
Georgia’s journey toward a sustainable, peaceful and resilient future hinges on fostering trust between communities divided by conflict and on ensuring access to essential services, viable livelihoods, and the full protection of human rights to all conflict-affected people.

planEntityVersion.description:
In Outcome 2 of the CF 2026-2030, the UN in Eswatini aims to foster an enabling environment for economic development, empowerment and livelihood diversification, contributing directly to poverty eradication and inclusive economic growth. This outcome supports the Government’s efforts to reduce
poverty (SDG 1), end hunger and achieve food security (SDG 2), and promote decent work and sustained economic growth (SDG 8). The UNCT will work with national institutions, the private sector, and civil society to strengthen value chains, enhance access to finance particularly for MSMEs and promote skills development aligned with market needs. These efforts will help unlock economic opportunities for vulnerable populations, including women, youth, and rural communities, ensuring that economic growth is both inclusive and sustainable.

planEntityVersion.name: By 2030, people in Eswatini are benefiting from efficient and resilient systems that deliver quality services, particularly for the vulnerable populations
planEntityVersion.description:
Between 2026 - 2030, the UN system in Eswatini, in close relationship with the Government and stakeholders, aims to deliver transformative development results that address the country's most pressing socio-economic challenges.
This outcome area seeks to strengthen the efficiency and resilience of systems to deliver quality services, particularly for the most vulnerable populations. This includes women, youth, PWD, PLHIV, key populations, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and children. The result reflects a commitment to strengthening public service delivery systems that are inclusive, shock-responsive, and rights-based. It supports progress across multiple SDGs, including health (SDG 3), education (SDG 4), gender equality (SDG 5), reduced inequalities (SDG 10), climate action (SDG 13), and peace, justice, and strong institutions (SDG 16). Through this outcome, the UNCT will help build a more equitable and resilient Eswatini, where no one is left behind and development gains are protected against future shocks.

Fortalecidas las capacidades de los gobiernos, sectores, instituciones, comunidades y las personas para la gestión integral de la reducción de riesgos de desastre en todas sus etapas y para incrementar la resiliencia climática, a fin de contribuir a un desarrollo sostenible, inclusivo y con equidad.

PRODUCTO 3.2. Fortalecidas las capacidades de gobiernos territoriales, instituciones, sectores productivos y de servicios, comunidades y personas para un desarrollo económico menos intenso en carbono, que promueva la adopción de principios de circularidad y una transición energética justa.

Fortalecidas las capacidades de gobiernos territoriales, instituciones, sectores productivos y de servicios, comunidades y personas para la gestión sostenible de los recursos naturales y el medioambiente, y la conservación de los ecosistemas, a fin de contribuir al desarrollo económico y social en interés público.

PRODUCTO 2.2. Fortalecidas capacidades y alianzas público-privadas, en interés público, de sectores estratégicos y cadenas de valor sostenibles e innovadoras, que fomenten exportaciones y/o sustituyan importaciones, con énfasis en los sectores alimentario, energético, biotecnológico, turístico y de industrias culturales y creativas, apoyando el empoderamiento económico de mujeres y jóvenes.

PRODUCTO 2.1. Fortalecido marco institucional y de políticas públicas habilitador de una transformación productiva soberana energéticamente, que promueva alianzas internacionales, inversiones, innovación, transformación digital, formación y trabajo digno y articulación de actores de conformidad con la legislación nacional, considerando la dinámica demográfica.

PRODUCTO 1.3. Instituciones fortalecen capacidades para la toma de decisiones de políticas públicas basadas en datos e información, que incluye las cuentas nacionales, la dinámica demográfica, e impulsando la transformación digital, teniendo en cuenta los principios de inclusión, igualdad y no discriminación.

PRODUCTO 1.2. Instituciones, autoridades locales y actores clave, de conformidad con la legislación nacional, cuentan con las competencias y capacidades fortalecidas para impulsar procesos de descentralización y desarrollo territorial, asegurando la articulación de actores de conformidad con la legislación nacional, la inclusión e igualdad de género, la participación con énfasis en jóvenes y la transparencia.

PRODUCTO 1.1. Instituciones y actores clave, de conformidad con la legislación nacional, desarrollan capacidades innovadoras para acceder a la financiación al desarrollo, modernizar las finanzas públicas y la gestión macroeconómica.

Gobierno eficaz:  Perfeccionar y modernizar la gestión pública a nivel nacional y local.

planEntityVersion.name: Increased coverage and sustainability of social protection programmes, and scaled up inclusive and quality community-based social services to meet the needs of vulnerable groups and protect them from all forms of violence
planEntityVersion.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework and reduction of barriers (geographical, financial, social) for access to quality social services 
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework, as well as specific policies related to the national child protection system strengthening
▪	Strengthening capacity for effective implementation of social assistance programmes among national and local organizations
▪	Strengthening the child protection governance structures, including coordination across government departments, between levels of decentralization and between formal and informal actors     
▪	Implementing structural changes in the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Population to roll out social protection services across the country, establishment of social protection directorates and departments in velayats and etraps. Expanding community-based social services and specialised services along with capacity building of social work specialists in each etrap.
▪	Strengthening the capacity of psychosocial support professionals and developing community-based services for young people 
▪	Strengthening rehabilitation centres under the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry as inclusive resource centres for cross-sectoral inclusive services for persons with disabilities (rehabilitation and habilitation, early intervention, inclusive education) in line with the ICF and CRPD. Promoting a multi-sectoral system of assistive technologies and products for people with disabilities as part of the national rehabilitation strategy 
▪	Introducing and expanding specialised support services for families with children, including reintegration services for families with children with disabilities and in difficult life situations 
▪	Increasing institutional capacity and improved referral systems and services to protect women and children from all forms of violence. Introducing a system of special services for child protection and prevention of child violence. Supporting systems to challenge social norms to achieve gender equality and eliminate all forms of gender-based violence 
▪	Strengthening a range of services and programmes available that prevent unnecessary separation from the family, including gatekeeping by competent authorities, awareness of the harms of institutionalisation of children, and family support services aimed at preventing separation
▪	Strengthening systems of reintegration support for returning migrants in vulnerable situations and their families through a case management approach across economic, social and psychological dimensions, taking into account their specific needs, vulnerability, age, gender as well as skills, knowledge and transnational networks they acquired in migration.
▪	Developing new social protection packages for different type disabilities (cash plus services) based on the additional costs associated with disability
▪	Strengthening inter-sectoral coordination and referral mechanisms to provide integrated services to vulnerable population groups

planEntityVersion.name: Low-carbon, inclusive and resilient growth
planEntityVersion.description: This strategic priority focuses on building a low-carbon, competitive and green economy for decent work and working conditions that are compliant with EU and other international standards and Multilateral Environmental Agreements.

planEntityVersion.name: The education system, from pre-primary to tertiary, provides quality, inclusive and safe learning opportunities for all children and young people, including children with disabilities
planEntityVersion.description:

●	Implementing a strategy to increase access to preschool education and early childhood development opportunities, including the diversification of preschool education by introducing a one-year half-day quality preschool education programme. 
●	Supporting the role of parents in early childhood development: Empowering and supporting parents to create rich learning and developmental experiences for children 
●	Implementing an inclusive education policy for children with disabilities in line with the national concept of inclusive education. Supporting the inclusion of children with disabilities in mainstream schools. Reform of the Medical and Pedagogical Commissions under the Ministry of Education in line with the ICF and CRPD (normative framework, orientations, data management, piloting) to support inclusive education and de-institutionalisation 
●	Strengthening educational (rehabilitation) centres under the Ministry of Education as resource centres to support inclusive education and intersectoral services for people with disabilities (transdisciplinary and interdisciplinary support, augmentative and alternative communication).
●	Introducing gender-sensitive and inclusive standards for safe learning spaces for children, covering prevention, response and victim support
●	Improving the mechanism for providing social services to vulnerable groups, including patients with TB and other infectious diseases.
●	Increased life skills training opportunities for young people, including positive masculinity norms for young men

planEntityVersion.name: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntityVersion.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Developing and implementing public health policies and programmes, and financing efficiency approaches to improve the quality of health services. Integrating essential social services into national urbanisation policies 
▪	Strengthening people-centred primary health care, including equitable access to quality health, products, medicines and vaccines, capacity of health workers, collection and analysis of health data 
▪	Strengthening maternal and child health, reproductive health and family planning services. Improving infant and young child nutrition, including breastfeeding and complementary feeding, early detection and intervention services. Integrating reproductive health into education systems in schools and beyond, including digital spaces. 
▪	Developing a digital health system 
▪	Implementing a ICD-11 implementation  roadmap and the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) in the health care system.  Reforming of medical and social expert assessment (regulatory framework, directions, data management, piloting) in accordance with the ICF 
▪	Strengthening the health system to combat NCDs (CVDs, diabetes, cancer, COPD and mental health) through prevention, screening, treatment, rehabilitation, palliative care and control of NCD risk factors 
▪	Strengthening the capacity of MHPSS frontline workers and developing services for young people and families
▪	Strengthening the health system to combat communicable diseases, including tuberculosis, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS and STIs, influenza, zoonoses 
▪	Strengthening the national programme for immunisation and control of VPI with focus on polio and acute flaccid paralysis, measles and rubella surveillance, including supply chain innovations
▪	Strengthening national capacities to implement the One Health approach
▪	Strengthening national capacities for risk prevention and reduction, strategic and operational preparedness and resilience, and effective response to health emergencies and those caused by all hazards, including pandemics
▪	Introducing behavioural and cultural approaches to improve health literacy, promote healthy lifestyles. Improving the nutrition of the entire population, including women of reproductive age and adolescent girls. Increasing public awareness of healthy diets, food and nutrition security and the gradual transition of production, distribution, retailing and consumption to more sustainable and resilient agri-food systems. 
▪	Promoting and supporting positive parenting through information, counselling, guidance and behavioural modelling, including through demonstration and practical sessions

planEntityVersion.name: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntityVersion.description:

▪	Assessing the policy, technology and financing situation for the green energy transition. Capacity building of technical experts and decision makers at all levels to develop and implement policies 
▪	Demonstrating approaches to rational use of land, water, forest and other natural resources
▪	Designing, constructing, and operationalizing green infrastructure
▪	Strengthening protected area management and biodiversity conservation through field-level interventions, such as eco-sensitive infrastructure, environmental monitoring systems, capacity building and ecotourism models that balance conservation and livelihoods.
▪	Implementation of effective methods for the management of protected areas and conservation of biodiversity

planEntityVersion.name: National climate early warning and DRR systems are aligned with the Sendai Framework for DRR and their capacities are strengthened

▪	Improving emergency preparedness and response capacity of relevant government agencies and non-governmental sector partners

▪	Supporting the National Action Plan to strengthen a social protection system capable of responding to emergencies. Strengthening the capacity of the health system and other relevant government agencies, including at border crossings to prevent, rapidly detect and effectively respond to all health emergencies
▪	Building resilience to climate change by strengthening people-centred, gender-sensitive and climate risk-sensitive knowledge base and capacities
▪	Improving sustainable urban and territorial planning and development to reduce risks and enhance resilience

planEntityVersion.name: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement

▪	Application of UNECE environmental conventions in Turkmenistan

planEntityVersion.description: Al 2030 Guatemala fortalece su gobernanza ambiental y promueve la inversión pública y privada sostenible, asegura el acceso equitativo de la población a sus beneficios, transforma sistemas agroalimentarios y refuerza la resiliencia ante riesgos ambientales y de origen natural, impulsa la participación y apropiación de las personas, con pertinencia cultural, fortalece y aplica el marco regulatorio para reducir la contaminación, la degradación de la biodiversidad y de los recursos naturales.

planEntityVersion.name: Contribuyendo al Desarrollo Humano: Lucha Contra la Pobreza y Generación de Prosperidad
planEntityVersion.description: Al 2030 las personas, especialmente las mujeres, jóvenes, y Pueblos Indígenas, amplían sus oportunidades para desarrollarse plenamente y participar activamente en una economía más diversificada, resiliente e inclusiva, que genere medios de vida sostenibles y trabajo decente, así como a sistemas de protección social, que incluyan un pilar de cuidados, y servicios públicos inclusivos de mejor calidad, oportunos, culturalmente pertinentes y con enfoque territorial.

planEntityVersion.name: Fortaleciendo la Gobernabilidad Democrática y el Estado de Derecho
planEntityVersion.description: Al 2030 las personas, especialmente las mujeres, jóvenes y Pueblos Indígenas, de los territorios más vulnerables, ejercen sus derechos humanos y su ciudadanía en condiciones de igualdad sustantiva, en el marco del Estado de Derecho y la gobernanza democrática, libre de discriminación y racismo, y que garantice una paz firme y duradera.
